newsitem.title: UK: Steam power hits Rolls-Royce year profits.
newsitem.headline: Steam power hits Rolls-Royce year profits.

text.p: Engines manufacturer Rolls-Royce Plc slipped into loss on Thursday, with underlying profits last year wiped out by its decision to withdraw from the steam power generation market.

The company reported a pretax loss of 28 million poundsrr. ($45.2 million) compared to a profit of 175 million pounds in 1995 after booking in 263 million pounds of provisions, write-offs and losses detailed in the half-year results for its plan to bale out of the steam power generation business. ($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
But it said operating profits from its core aero-engines and industrial power businesses rose to 242 million pounds ($390.3 million) from 178 million pounds in 1995, boosted by strong order books.
Annual sales excluding businesses to be sold rose to 4.05 billion pounds from 3.34 billon pounds a year ago.
The final dividend was raised 10 percent to 3.3 pence a share, making 5.3 pence for the year against 5.0 pence last time, on pre-exceptional earnings of 12.7 pence, up from 7.94 pence in 1995.
"We have continued to improve our underlying financial performance," chairman Sir Ralph Robins said in the results statement.
"We are confident that the actions we have taken and the strategies we are pursuing leave us well positioned to build a strong future." ($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
